title: Why AI data centers became an electricity bill fight
description: AI runs in power-hungry data centers, and communities are arguing over who pays for the grid upgrades. Here's how a chat answer ends up on the grid.

scenes.say: AI runs in data centers, and those data centers are now at the center of an electricity bill fight.
You send a prompt. Thousands of chips in a data center work out the answer. Those chips give off heat, so cooling takes power too. And it all comes from the local grid.

A Bloomberg analysis found wholesale electricity prices near some data centers rose as much as two hundred sixty-seven percent over five years. Cornell researchers estimate operators cover about thirty-eight percent of the grid costs tied to their growth.
Supporters point to investment and tax revenue, and some big companies have pledged to cover their own power costs. Critics worry about higher bills, noise, and land use.
A Gallup poll in March found seventy-one percent of Americans oppose a data center in their area. Follow for the tech behind the headlines.
